subject.title: fix(plugin-sdk): update ssrf-runtime import path in cdp-proxy-bypass

question: Should the `fetchConfiguredLocalOriginWithSsrFGuard` and `registerManagedProxyBrowserCdpBypass` helpers become public `ssrf-runtime` SDK exports, or should the fix preserve owner-scoped/private Browser/Ollama access?
rationale: Both choices can address the package-subpath regression, but only maintainers can decide whether these SSRF/local-proxy bypass helpers are safe and intended as a public plugin contract.

options.title: Preserve owner-scoped private access
options.body: Repair the packaged Browser/Ollama load path through the existing private bundled-plugin mechanism or another narrow private seam without adding these helpers to the public SSRF barrel.

options.title: Promote the SDK surface deliberately
options.body: Land the public export approach only with matching docs, contract/baseline updates, guardrail changes, and package smoke proof that maintainers explicitly accept.

options.title: Pause for canonical direction
options.body: Hold this branch while maintainers choose between this public-barrel approach and sibling private-subpath compatibility approaches for the canonical regression.

recommendation.title: Preserve owner-scoped private access
recommendation.body: Repair the packaged Browser/Ollama load path through the existing private bundled-plugin mechanism or another narrow private seam without adding these helpers to the public SSRF barrel.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision centers on the package-boundary hardening and private SDK declaration policy connected to `steipete`'s prior commit.
